action.rationale: Fresh problem and budget 100 is below the 20·dim=120 threshold for full probing at dim=6, so I’ll run lightweight probes P1–P3 (~12 evals) to gauge smoothness and global structure. These evaluations seed the archive for warm starts on this cheap, deterministic problem.

Budget is small (100 < 20·dim=120) and probes were light (8 evals). P2 shows weak global structure (fdc_spearman=0.19, top10_spread_vs_uniform=1.09) and P3 is unavailable, so it’s ambiguous which global method will do better. Race cma_es vs turbo for 18 evals (~20% of remaining) to pick the stronger approach before committing the rest.

Probes indicate weak global structure (P2 fdc_spearman = 0.1905, top10_spread_vs_uniform = 1.091), favoring a population method. CMA-ES just won the race (best 0.3149 from 0.3230) and is only at generation 1 with sigma 0.284, so it deserves a full round. With 74 evals left, continuing CMA-ES now is the most sample-efficient next step before considering restarts or polish.

CMA-ES just improved from 0.3149 to 0.2973 over 30 evals (improvement 0.0176) and is not converged (sigma 0.239, converged=false; stall_evals 7 < 2×round_size). With 44 evals left, another CMA-ES round is likely to yield more gains while still leaving room for a short polish.

Only 14 evaluations remain (86/100 used) and CMA-ES has stalled for 37 evals without improvement (best 0.297346 since eval 49), so exploring further is unlikely to pay off. Polishing from the active best with L-BFGS-B is the fastest local refinement on smooth deterministic problems in dim=6, whereas BOBYQA would spend ~13 evals just to start. This targets a final gain before the budget ends.

Only 7 evaluations remain (93/100 used) and lbfgsb has exhausted at the incumbent with 0 improvement in its 7-eval tenure; stall_evals is 44. Further local polish is unlikely and BOBYQA would need ≥13 evals (2·dim+1) to even start, so stopping avoids wasting time.
